profile.reading:
The Terminal Commerce Building stands at 401 North Broad Street in Philadelphia's Callowhill neighborhood, a fourteen story Art Deco front section paired with a twelve story, H shaped rear warehouse, together totaling more than 1.3 million square feet on a footprint of roughly 528 by 225 feet. It was built between 1929 and 1931 by the Reading Company, the railroad that once anchored this stretch of North Broad Street, as a combined office, showroom, parking garage, warehouse, and freight station serving the company's rail and commercial operations. The building was designed by Steele, William and Sons Co. with reinforced concrete, brick, and terra cotta construction, including a central tower topped with terra cotta ornamented water tanks. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1996 as a contributing property within the Callowhill Industrial Historic District.

Netrality Properties acquired the building in March 2014 and has operated it since as a carrier neutral colocation and interconnection facility. Netrality's own marketing describes it as one of the East Coast's most fiber rich data centers, with more than 70 on network carriers and cloud providers, including direct access to major public cloud platforms, inside a carrier neutral meet me room environment. The company markets the building alongside its data center role as mixed use space, meaning it continues to combine leased office and commercial space with the data center and interconnection floors, an echo of the building's original multi purpose design as a railroad company's office, warehouse, and freight hub. Netrality has cited esports and gaming infrastructure company Nerd Street Gamers as one tenant benefiting from the building's direct connectivity.

No public source breaks out the building's dedicated data center square footage separately from its total 1.3 million square feet, nor does Netrality publish a power capacity figure in megawatts for the site. That level of disclosure is typical for large carrier hotels housed inside historic mixed use buildings, where the interconnection business occupies specific floors within a much larger structure rather than a purpose built, single tenant shell. What is well established is the building's status as a major regional interconnection point, commonly described in industry coverage as the most fiber dense, network neutral facility between New York and Virginia, a role that traces directly back to its scale, its central Philadelphia location, and the historic infrastructure the Reading Company built into it nearly a century ago.

reading.body:
Terminal Commerce Building in Philadelphia is a historic 1.3 million square foot structure built in 1929-1931 and now operated as a colocation and interconnection facility by Netrality Properties. The facility is described by its operator as the most fiber dense, network neutral data center between New York and Virginia, and sits in a state where only four of fourteen mapped data center facilities publish power specifications. No megawatt figure is published for this campus, so its actual computational capacity cannot be assessed from available data.

The absence of a published power specification for Terminal Commerce Building makes it impossible to determine whether it ranks among Pennsylvania's significant AI infrastructure or represents modest colocation capacity. The state context shows this facility is the fifth largest by published megawatts, but that ranking applies only to the four facilities that have disclosed power figures; the true ranking is unknown. Of Pennsylvania's 22.2 megawatts of published data center capacity across all facilities, the contribution of Terminal Commerce Building remains unpublished.

Without a published power budget, this campus cannot be evaluated for its role in AI scaling. Whether it matters to AI infrastructure depends on specifications Netrality Properties has chosen not to disclose.
